verdict: Official jQuery 3.7.1 (slim) — a legitimate, widely used DOM library with no exfiltration or malicious behavior.
summary: This is the standard minified jQuery slim build. Its file size, structure, and public API (jQuery.fn, ajaxTransport, DOMEval) match the official release. It contains no outbound data collection, no obfuscation, and no attacker-controlled sinks. The only items of note are the library's own DOM APIs, which are only risky if application code feeds them untrusted input.

text: Provides DOM traversal, manipulation, and event helpers via the jQuery/$ API.
Exposes .html()/.append() which set innerHTML internally; risk depends entirely on what the host application passes in.
Includes an XMLHttpRequest-based ajax transport used only when the application calls $.ajax; makes no network requests on its own.

title: Recognized as official jQuery 3.7.1 slim
impact: No security concern from the library itself. Confirms provenance so reviewers can focus on application code and integrity, not the library internals.
recommendation: Pin the version and add Subresource Integrity (SRI) to the <script> tag to guarantee the delivered file is unmodified.

title: innerHTML setters are safe only with trusted input
impact: If application code passes untrusted strings to .html()/.append(), it can introduce DOM XSS. This is a property of how the app uses jQuery, not a flaw in jQuery.
recommendation: Review application calls to .html()/.append() and use .text() for untrusted data.

title: DOMEval / script creation is internal and benign
impact: This runs code jQuery already controls (e.g. inline scripts in appended HTML). It is not fed external input and matches the upstream source, so it is not exploitable on its own.
recommendation: No action beyond keeping the library up to date.

pci: Acceptable on payment pages when loaded with SRI and version pinning. jQuery itself neither reads cardholder data nor transmits anything; PCI DSS 6.4.3/11.6.1 concerns reduce to integrity of the delivered file.
privacy: No personal data collection, tracking, or fingerprinting. No GDPR/CCPA impact from the library itself.

text: Safe to keep. Load a pinned version from a trusted origin or self-host.
Add SRI (integrity + crossorigin) to the script tag to detect CDN tampering.
Audit application-level .html()/.append() usage for untrusted input to prevent DOM XSS.

policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' code.jquery.com; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'
notes: No 'unsafe-eval' or 'unsafe-inline' required; the slim build works under a strict policy.
